IR.rationale: A steepening US curve signals improving global growth expectations and reflation. These favour cyclical-heavy non-US equity markets over the following weeks.

B.rationale: Narrowing spreads together with strong high-yield returns describe easing credit conditions. Credit markets tend to lead equities in pricing global risk appetite.

V.rationale: Elevated implied volatility embeds a high variance and equity risk premium. Documented evidence links this to higher subsequent equity returns.

AP.rationale: Joint strength in US and emerging equities marks a global risk-on state. Lead-lag effects from the US market carry information to other developed markets at weekly frequency.

ST.rationale: Strong profitability-factor returns indicate flight to quality within equities. This signals a defensive regime that tends to coincide with weaker broad-market returns.

FX.rationale: A weakening dollar eases global financial conditions and raises the dollar value of foreign equity. Both channels support non-US index returns.

COM.rationale: Rising broad commodity prices reflect global demand strength. Commodity returns co-move with cyclical non-US equity markets.

MC.rationale: Tight financial conditions are associated with depressed prices and higher required returns. The state therefore carries information on subsequent returns.

ENDG.rationale: Time-series momentum at multi-week horizons, partly offset by short-term reversal, makes the index's own recent return informative.

IR.rationale: Abrupt rises in short rates signal hawkish policy surprises. These tighten global funding conditions and raise future equity variance.

B.rationale: Widening spreads with falling high-yield prices mark rising default and liquidity risk. This state precedes higher equity volatility.

V.rationale: Implied volatility forecasts realised variance beyond its own history. Policy uncertainty adds a persistent uncertainty component that spills over to global equity markets.

AP.rationale: Through the leverage and volatility-feedback effects, negative market returns raise subsequent volatility more than positive ones.

ST.rationale: High reversal-factor returns indicate scarce liquidity provision and price pressure. Such conditions coincide with turbulent, high-variance markets.

FX.rationale: A strengthening yen alongside a weakening Australian dollar is a carry-trade unwind and safe-haven state. It is associated with rising global equity volatility.

COM.rationale: Sharp oil declines often reflect global demand fears and stress in energy credit. Both raise equity uncertainty.

MC.rationale: Elevated financial stress, including funding and volatility components, predicts higher subsequent realised variance.

ENDG.rationale: Volatility clustering is nonlinear. Very high recent variance can carry persistence beyond what a linear own-variance term captures.

IR.rationale: Falling intermediate yields relative to the policy rate reflect flight to safety and downgraded growth expectations. This is a risk-off state.

B.rationale: Deteriorating credit conditions signal rising default risk and deleveraging. These raise the probability of an equity crash.

V.rationale: High implied volatility widens the return distribution. It also reflects demand for crash protection, making large losses more likely.

AP.rationale: Simultaneous weakness in US and emerging equities signals a global sell-off. Such sell-offs tend to propagate to developed non-US markets.

ST.rationale: Momentum drawdowns occur in panic states with sharp market reversals. They coincide with fragile, high-downside environments.

FX.rationale: A surging dollar together with a strengthening yen is the classic safe-haven, risk-off currency pattern. It also lowers the dollar value of foreign equities.

COM.rationale: Falling commodity prices point to weakening global demand. They hit cyclical and resource-heavy non-US markets.

MC.rationale: Financial stress combined with deteriorating labour data marks a stress-plus-recession state. This is where equity tail losses concentrate.

ENDG.rationale: Recent losses raise volatility through the leverage effect and can cascade. This makes further large losses more likely.

IR.rationale: Curve steepening reflects improving growth and reflation expectations. These can trigger strong cyclical equity rallies.

B.rationale: Strong returns in both high-yield and EM sovereign bonds signal a broad return of risk appetite. Large equity rebounds tend to accompany such states.

V.rationale: High-volatility regimes fatten both tails. The largest equity gains typically occur as rebounds while volatility is elevated.

AP.rationale: Strong emerging equity returns indicate global risk-on flows. Such flows tend to extend to developed non-US markets.

ST.rationale: Momentum crashes coincide with violent rebounds of beaten-down stocks. This marks rebound states with large market gains.

FX.rationale: A weakening dollar with a strengthening risk-sensitive currency is a global risk-on state. It also boosts dollar-measured foreign equity returns.

COM.rationale: Commodity rallies signal improving global demand. That favours large gains in cyclical non-US markets.

MC.rationale: When financial conditions are tight, prices are depressed and risk premia high. Relief can produce outsized rebounds.

ENDG.rationale: After sharp declines, short-horizon reversal and elevated volatility raise the chance of a large rebound.
